tasks.short: Price and file prescriptions that have been filled.

steps.what: Read the filled prescriptions on the counter.
Decide the price when the list has no line.
Tell the patient the price and take payment.
Write the price on the filled prescription line.
File the filled prescriptions in the drawer.
Post that price line onto the pharmacy record.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} copies the price line she wrote, with prescription id, article code, quantity, price and patient share, into the pharmacy record in {OTHER}. A blank line posts nothing, and a later change to that line voids the post. She still reads the filled prescription, decides a price the tariff list does not hold, tells the patient the price, takes payment, and files the paper script.
tasks.previous_blocker: The price sat on the paper script and was typed again into the pharmacy record, and a wrong price is a billing error.
tasks.enabler_now: The pharmacy record already stores a prescription line, so a flow can copy the fields she has just written. No new pricing engine.
tasks.still_hard: A pack with no tariff, a patient who pays at the counter, and the paper script in the drawer stay with her. The interaction and dose check stays with the pharmacist.
tasks.human_edge: She can see the pack in her hand and tell the patient what they owe.
tasks.altitude: She still prices the odd script and takes payment. She stops typing the same price a second time.

reach.task: Check interactions and dose before the medicine is handed out
reach.learn: Which missing tariff to bring to the pharmacist instead of guessing a price

evidence.claim: After a prescription is filled, the technician matches it to a tariff, tells the patient the amount, takes payment when they pay at the counter, and files the script. Model knowledge.
Dutch pharmacy systems run G-Standaard surveillance of interactions, contra-indications and dose, with KNMP minimum settings. This task does not do that check.
The medical dossier is kept for 20 years, and a patient may ask who viewed it.
Health data are a special category under GDPR article 9.

Under Dutch works-council rules, WOR article 27(1)(l), recording consultations or logging coder corrections can count as staff monitoring. A price-post log is not named there; treating it the same way is model knowledge.

assumptions: The tariff list (article code, tariff, patient-share rule) is kept by the pharmacist in the pharmacy record. It already exists. Its upkeep is not her saving. She reads it in s2. The machine does not look it up.

The price line she writes in s4 is the only structured input the post uses: prescription id, article code, quantity, price, patient share. That capture stays in s4 at full time. A blank line posts nothing.
Filling the medicine is an earlier task. This task starts from a filled prescription. If the prescription id is missing, she keeps the paper in the drawer and s6 does not run.
Telling the patient the price and taking payment are unchanged. Filing the paper script in the drawer is unchanged.
The post log stores the prescription id and the time. It is not a score of her speed. Works-council consent follows national rules before that log is switched on.
Focal upkeep is the small allowance below for lines the record rejects. It is not zero.
unknowns: Whether this pharmacy's record already copies a confirmed price without a second keying.
Whether patients pay at this counter or the insurer is billed later.
Whether the volume of prescription lines counts as large-scale health-data processing.
research_questions: What share of filled scripts has no tariff line and is priced by hand?
Does the paper script still have to be stored, or is the pharmacy record the dossier?

already_counted.description: Writing the price line before it is posted

incremental.description: Clear price lines the pharmacy record rejects
Pharmacist keeps article tariffs on the tariff list

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most scripts have no tariff or no prescription id, she prices and files them by hand, and the post does not run. High: the line she wrote is complete and only the second keying disappears. The counter conversation, the payment and the drawer stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Order, label and count stock, then enter the count.

steps.what: Count the medications, chemicals and supplies on the shelf.
Decide which stock to order from that count.
Label the medication containers by hand.
Write the item, the count and the order quantity.
Order that stock from the supplier.
Enter that count on the pharmacy inventory computer.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} copies the count line she wrote, item id, quantity counted and quantity to order, into the pharmacy inventory record in {OTHER}. There is no par level and no automatic reorder. She still counts the shelf, decides the order, labels the packs, and places the order with the supplier by phone or on the {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The count was on a sheet and typed again, and a wrong stock figure can leave a medicine short.
tasks.enabler_now: The inventory record already accepts an item and a quantity, so the second keying can be a copy of the line she wrote.
tasks.still_hard: Counting, labelling and choosing how much to order stay physical and local. A pack with no item id does not enter itself.
tasks.human_edge: She is the person who can see the shelf and the damaged or unlabelled pack.
tasks.altitude: The shelf round is unchanged. She no longer keys the same count into the computer after writing it down.

reach.task: Decide which medicines must not run out overnight
reach.learn: Which short count to order now rather than on the next round

evidence.claim: The technician counts and labels stock by hand, decides what to order, places that order, and types the count into the inventory record. Model knowledge. This design uses no par level.
Health data are a special category under GDPR article 9. A shelf line with only item and quantity is not a patient record unless a patient is named on it. That limit is model knowledge.
Under Dutch works-council rules, WOR article 27(1)(l), logging how staff correct records can count as staff monitoring. The inventory post is not named there.

assumptions: There is no par level. She decides the quantity to order in s2. Nothing calculates a reorder point.

The count line she writes in s4 is the structured input the computer entry uses: item id copied from the pack, quantity counted, quantity to order. That writing stays at full time. A blank line is not entered.

The supplier catalogue (supplier id, supplier item code, pack size) is kept by the purchasing clerk. It is not her saving. She still places the order herself in s5. The machine does not send the order.
If the pack has no item id, she writes the name, s6 does not run, and she keys that line herself. The range low is that case.
Focal upkeep is the small allowance for lines the inventory record rejects.
unknowns: Whether item ids on the packs match the inventory record in this pharmacy.
Whether orders go by phone, by portal, or both.
research_questions: What share of packs have an item id she can copy onto the count line?
Who is allowed to change a stock figure after she has written it?

already_counted.description: Writing the count line before it is entered

incremental.description: Fix inventory lines the record does not recognise
Purchasing clerk keeps the supplier item list

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: packs have no item id, she still types every count, and the copy does not run. High: she has written a complete count line and only the second keying into the inventory computer disappears. Counting, labelling, deciding and placing the order stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compute charges for dispensed medication and enter them.

steps.what: Read the medication or equipment dispensed to hospital patients.
Decide charges the tariff list cannot price.
Write those charges for the unresolved medication lines.
Compute charges from the dispensed pharmacy record and tariff.
Check the computed charges for those hospital patients.
Enter the checked charges into the billing record.

tasks.design: Where the pharmacy dispense record in {OTHER} already holds patient id, article code, quantity and date, and the tariff list in the {ERP} holds a tariff for that article, the {WORKFLOW} multiplies quantity by tariff and drafts the charge. It skips a row that lacks either field. She still reads what was dispensed to the hospital patients, prices the gaps by hand, and checks that the medicine name, the quantity and the amount match. The {WORKFLOW} enters only the charge she checked.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quantity and tariff lived in two records, and she multiplied and retyped them onto the patient bill.
tasks.enabler_now: Both fields are structured when they exist, so the multiplication is ordinary arithmetic. No model is required.
tasks.still_hard: A missing quantity or a missing tariff, and the check that the charge is for the right medicine, stay with her. A wrong charge is a billing error.
tasks.human_edge: She can see that the charge names the medicine that was actually dispensed, not only that the amount equals quantity times tariff.
tasks.altitude: She still opens the odd dispense and releases every charge. Complete rows are multiplied for her.

reach.task: Post patient charges onto the hospital bill
reach.learn: Which charge codes the ward bill will accept

evidence.claim: A hospital charge for a dispensed medicine is the quantity dispensed times a tariff, then entered on the patient bill. Model knowledge. No coding-rate or robot-output figure is used as this task's saving.
Health data are a special category under GDPR article 9.
Large-scale processing needs a data protection impact assessment.
The medical dossier is kept for 20 years, and a patient may ask who viewed it.

Software with a medical purpose is a medical device. This design multiplies a stored quantity by a stored tariff and does not recommend a dose. Whether that is a medical purpose is not settled by the source.

assumptions: The dispense record is produced when the medicine or equipment is handed out, in an earlier task, by the pharmacy technician or the pharmacist. Fields: patient id, article code, quantity, date. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as saved here. If quantity, article or patient id is missing, the compute skips the row.

The tariff list is kept by the pharmacist with finance in the {ERP}: article code, charge code, tariff amount. Its upkeep is other-role time, not her saving. If the article has no tariff, the compute skips the row.

Skipped rows are the ones she decides in s2 and writes in s3: patient id, article code, quantity, tariff, charge code. That writing stays at full time. The compute does not read her note and does not invent a tariff.
She checks the draft in s5 before anything is entered: the medicine name matches the dispense line, the quantity matches, and the amount is quantity times tariff. A rejected draft is not entered.
The enter step posts only the checked charge. It does not calculate a new amount.
Focal upkeep is the allowance for charges the billing record rejects.
unknowns: Whether dispense quantity and the tariff list are complete for this hospital's wards.
Whether this volume of patient charges is large-scale health-data processing.
Whether a regulator would treat the multiplier as medical-purpose software.
research_questions: What share of dispense rows lacks a quantity or a tariff?
Who may reverse a charge after it is on the patient bill?

already_counted.description: Checking computed and handwritten charges before they are entered

incremental.description: Rework charges the billing record rejects
Pharmacist and finance keep the tariff list

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most rows lack a quantity or a tariff, she prices them by hand, and the multiplier rarely runs; a little of the final enter still copies a charge she has already checked. High: most rows are complete, so the multiplication and the enter of checked lines go, while reading and the check stay. This is not a coding-rate or a robot-output figure.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and process medical insurance claim forms.

steps.what: Read the insurance claim forms and the records.
Decide which claim lines the insurer can take.
Write the missing claim fields onto the form line.
Prepare insurance claim forms from the pharmacy record.
Check the claim forms against the medication records.
Process the checked claim forms to the insurer channel.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} fills a fixed claim form from the pharmacy record in {OTHER} and from the gap fields she wrote: patient id, insurer id, prescription id, article, quantity, amount and date. A missing field leaves the form blank. No model reads the paper. She still reads the form, decides which lines the insurer can take, and checks that the medicine, quantity, amount and date match the filled prescription. The {WORKFLOW} sends only the form she checked, on the insurer channel in {OTHER}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Claim forms were paper, fields were copied by hand, and sending the wrong medicine or amount is hard to undo.
tasks.enabler_now: When the priced prescription and the insurer id are already fields, filling the form is a template copy. A model is not required.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding what the insurer will accept, and checking the medicine against the prescription, stay with her. A rejected claim comes back as her rework.
tasks.human_edge: She can see that the form names the medicine that was dispensed and the insurer that covers that patient.
tasks.altitude: She still reads each claim and releases the send. She stops copying complete fields onto the form by hand.

reach.task: Keep the insurer identifier on the patient record
reach.learn: Which missing insurer field stops a claim from being prepared

evidence.claim: Insurance claim forms are prepared from the priced prescription and sent to the insurer. Model knowledge. A hospital coding rate is not this task's saving, and no model reads the form.
Health data are a special category under GDPR article 9.
Large-scale processing needs a data protection impact assessment.
The medical dossier is kept for 20 years, and a patient may ask who viewed it.

Software with a medical purpose is a medical device. This design copies claim fields and does not recommend a treatment. Whether a regulator would still call the form filler a device is not settled by the source.
Under Dutch works-council rules, WOR article 27(1)(l), logging how staff correct records can count as staff monitoring. A claim-send log is not named there.

assumptions: The priced prescription is produced when the prescription is priced and filed, outside this task: patient id, prescription id, article code, quantity, amount, date. That capture is not counted as saved here. If any of those fields is missing, the form stays blank.

The insurer id is kept on the patient record by the medical records specialist. That upkeep is other-role time. If the insurer id is missing, she writes it in s3, and that writing stays at full time. Fields she writes: insurer id and any amount or date the priced record lacks.
The prepare step copies only those fields onto a fixed form. It does not read free text and it does not invent a code. A blank required field produces no form.
She checks the draft before it is sent: medicine name, quantity, amount and date match the filled prescription, and the insurer id is the patient's insurer. A failed check is not sent.
The send posts the checked form only. A change after the check voids the send.
The send log stores the claim id and the time, not a score of her speed. Works-council consent follows national rules.
Focal upkeep is the allowance for claims the insurer returns.
unknowns: Whether this insurer takes a structured batch or still wants a paper form.
Whether insurer ids are already on the patient record.
Whether this claim volume is large-scale health-data processing.
The national layout of the claim form.
research_questions: What share of claim forms is missing an insurer id or an amount?
Who may withdraw a claim after it has been sent?

already_counted.description: Checking the claim form against the prescription before it is sent

incremental.description: Medical records specialist keeps insurer ids on the patient record

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: insurer ids and amounts are missing, she still prepares the forms by hand, and only a few checked forms are sent by the flow. High: the priced record and the insurer id are present, so form-filling and the send of checked forms go, while reading, deciding and the check stay. No coding-rate figure is used.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still the counter, the shelf and the odd charge. She stops typing a second copy of a price, a count, a complete charge or a complete claim.
reach: Pharmacist: which missing tariff or odd pack to escalate before a price or a charge is posted.
Medical records specialist: which insurer fields must sit on the patient record before a claim form can be filled.
skills_to_grow: Match a pack to the tariff line instead of inventing a price.
Write a count line with item, quantity counted and quantity to order so the shelf count is not keyed twice.
Spot a claim whose medicine, quantity or amount does not match the filled prescription.
role.ambitious_version: She still counts, labels, takes payment and releases every charge and claim. A second copy is posted only from fields she wrote or from a dispense row and a tariff that already exist, and a blank field posts nothing.
